items.stem: Why is retrieval grounding valuable in a customer-support chatbot?

options.text: It bases answers on the company's actual help content, reducing fabrication
options.rationale: Correct: grounding in source content keeps answers accurate and current.

options.text: It makes the model forget the conversation
options.rationale: Grounding supplies sources; it does not erase conversation state.

options.text: It removes the need for any safety controls
It guarantees the bot never needs a human
options.rationale: Escalation is still needed for some cases.

items.explanation: Correct: grounding in source content keeps answers accurate and current.

items.stem: Which TWO are important design elements for a production customer chatbot? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A fallback or escalation path when the bot is unsure
options.rationale: Correct: safe fallback and human escalation handle cases the bot cannot.

options.text: Monitoring of live conversations for quality and failures
options.rationale: Correct: production monitoring catches regressions and abuse.

options.text: Resending the full chat history on every turn regardless of length
options.rationale: That overflows context and wastes cost; state must be managed.

options.text: Answering only from the model's memory with no sources

items.explanation: Correct: safe fallback and human escalation handle cases the bot cannot.

items.stem: A chatbot's prompts grow until they exceed the context window as conversations get long. What is the standard fix?

options.text: Summarise or truncate older turns to keep the working context in budget
options.rationale: Correct: managing state via summarisation keeps conversations within the window.

options.text: Switch to a stateless single call

options.rationale: Temperature does not change context length.
Disabling grounding harms accuracy and does not fix context size.

items.explanation: Correct: managing state via summarisation keeps conversations within the window.
